title: Windows Vault credential store
whyItMatters: The Vault holds encrypted web and Windows credentials. Its size shows how many secrets the account saved that need rotating before handover.
source: DPAPI and Credential Manager reference: Windows Vault at %LOCALAPPDATA%/Microsoft/Vault - https://www.windowsforensics.app/en/artifacts/dpapi-credential-manager
notes: Contains per-GUID vault folders with encrypted .vcrd files. No vault file is opened or decrypted; a roaming copy under APPDATA is not covered here.

cleanup.exportFirst: Write down the passwords held in the Vault, because vault entries cannot be exported before they are removed.
cleanup.signOut: Sign out of the Microsoft account and apps whose credentials are stored in the Vault on this PC.
steps: Open Credential Manager from the Start menu and select Windows Credentials.
Remove each vault entry you no longer need.
Do not delete the folder named in the plan by hand; removing entries in Credential Manager is enough, and the full reset clears the rest.
cleanup.risk: Removes saved web and Windows credentials from the Vault; apps using them will ask for a password again.
cleanup.source: Microsoft Support, Credential Manager in Windows: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/credential-manager-in-windows
